I am using Samsung after a long time. Especially, I have never used Samsung android before. And now I don’t want to use other android phones at all. One UI is really a charm. Lots of customisations, user-friendliness and a clean UI, that’s what I can tell about Samsung’s One UI, and once you start using this with its useful features, you get used to this, and you don’t want to switch. Now I understand why people who used Samsung android once in their life don’t want to go to another brand. At least, I don’t want to switch very soon.Now coming to the phone. I have got this for Rs. 34000/- during the Big Billion Day sale.Battery: My main concern was the battery, and this is the reason I didn’t go for S23 FE, which was available at almost the same price. The battery in the A55 is better than the one in S23 FE. In fact, I would say that this is one of the longest running batteries in the market. It gives you almost 6.5 hours of screen on time, if you charge it to 100%. I charge it to 80%, which is good for the battery, and you can set this in settings. The battery will stop charging once it reaches 80%. Set that and your battery will be healthy for more years.Build Quality: The reason I didn’t go for the A35. Both are designed the same, but the A55 has an Aluminium frame. It makes it a bit heavier, but is definitely worth it. I admit that the Aluminium frame isn’t visible if you use a case, which you should do, but it adds to the phone’s durability. And I intend to use this for at least 4-5 years, so durability is a big thing for this phone.Display: I think I don’t need to say much about Samsung’s display. It has a 120Hz SAMOLED screen, which is very beautiful. You can limit the refresh rate to 60Hz, it consumes less battery, but looks equally awesome.Update Policy: Samsung promises to provide 4 years of Android updates and 5 years of Security updates. I think Samsung will keep their promise, and I will be able to use this phone for up to 6 years without any concern.Camera: Camera isn’t one of the USPs of this phone, mostly for the redundant Macro sensor. The Macro sensor isn’t very good. They could easily replace it with a telephoto lens, but then no one would buy the S23 FE. The 50MP main camera and the 12MP ultrawide lens is good. Low light photography is also very good with this camera. I guess its not possible to upgrade a Macro lens through updates, so you have to sacrifice the telephoto lens for good battery life.Adaptability: Last, but not the least, this phone adapts to your usage. You will feel this after a few days of usage, and it feels very good.The Samsung Galaxy A55 is a good budget phone, if you prefer battery life and durability over telephoto zoom lens.

I am using Samsung after a long time. Especially, I have never used Samsung android before. And now I don’t want to use other android phones at all. One UI is really a charm. Lots of customisations, user-friendliness and a clean UI, that’s what I can tell about Samsung’s One UI, and once you start using this with its useful features, you get used to this, and you don’t want to switch. Now I understand why people who used Samsung android once in their life don’t want to go to another brand. At least, I don’t want to switch very soon.Now coming to the phone. I have got this for Rs. 34000/- during the Big Billion Day sale.Battery: My main concern was the battery, and this is the reason I didn’t go for S23 FE, which was available at almost the same price. The battery in the A55 is better than the one in S23 FE. In fact, I would say that this is one of the longest running batteries in the market. It gives you almost 6.5 hours of screen on time, if you charge it to 100%. I charge it to 80%, which is good for the battery, and you can set this in settings. The battery will stop charging once it reaches 80%. Set that and your battery will be healthy for more years.Build Quality: The reason I didn’t go for the A35. Both are designed the same, but the A55 has an Aluminium frame. It makes it a bit heavier, but is definitely worth it. I admit that the Aluminium frame isn’t visible if you use a case, which you should do, but it adds to the phone’s durability. And I intend to use this for at least 4-5 years, so durability is a big thing for this phone.Display: I think I don’t need to say much about Samsung’s display. It has a 120Hz SAMOLED screen, which is very beautiful. You can limit the refresh rate to 60Hz, it consumes less battery, but looks equally awesome.Update Policy: Samsung promises to provide 4 years of Android updates and 5 years of Security updates. I think Samsung will keep their promise, and I will be able to use this phone for up to 6 years without any concern.Camera: Camera isn’t one of the USPs of this phone, mostly for the redundant Macro sensor. The Macro sensor isn’t very good. They could easily replace it with a telephoto lens, but then no one would buy the S23 FE. The 50MP main camera and the 12MP ultrawide lens is good. Low light photography is also very good with this camera. I guess its not possible to upgrade a Macro lens through updates, so you have to sacrifice the telephoto lens for good battery life.Adaptability: Last, but not the least, this phone adapts to your usage. You will feel this after a few days of usage, and it feels very good.The Samsung Galaxy A55 is a good budget phone, if you prefer battery life and durability over telephoto zoom lens.

This is more of a service review than a product review. Hope it helps anyone who wants to order high-value items from Amazon. I'm an Amazon Prime member. If this was the experience we had, I can only imagine what non-Prime members go through. We ordered this item on 12th October. The initial delivery was quick. The nightmare began once we received the item. First of all, we were not contacted by the installation team within the timeframe claimed by Amazon. We raised a request with Customer Care for installation. The installation team then figured out that the product was incompatible. The exact reason was that the second door had dimensions that were mismatched to the refrigerator cubicle and therefore would not seal on closing. Therefore we were not able to start the fridge operation. Thereafter, the installation team, instead of going ahead and declaring the item as non-operational and ordering a replacement/refund for us, instructed us to raise the request with Amazon. Once we raised a defective item request with Amazon, the same team took more than 2 days to arrive and declare the item as defective. On declaration, they asked us to speak to Amazon again for the return of this item. The return team again inspected the item thoroughly and picked it up for return. In the meantime, Amazon informed us that they cannot ship the replacement to us, even though the above item was marked defective by their own installation team, and they even signed off on it, until they receive the returned product. The product was picked up on 17th October, and it still hasn't reached Amazon. In the meantime, they held us, hostage, by not shipping the replacement product to date. Ultimately, we had to cancel the replacement because customer service let us know that they may receive the item only in the week of 30th October, and thereafter, it may take a week for the replacement to be shipped to us. Moreover, for the cancellation, they informed us that regardless of the timeframe, they will be able to process our cancellation only after they receive the item at their warehouse. My question to Amazon/vendor is: (1) What was our fault as customers that the item turned out to be defective due to the poor performance/inadequacy of your quality control team and why should we be punished for it? (2) As a Fortune 10 company, since this is a failure at your end, shouldn't you try to pacify the customer, who has paid the due amount in full (Rs. 30990/-) and make sure that they do not go through any hassles, provided they already faced one due to the defective item? Isn't that in your customer satisfaction ethos? (3) Once your installation team and pick up team have verified the item as defective, shouldn't you process the cancellation order (in case the customer desires a cancellation over replacement) based on your team's verification instead of waiting to receive the item at your warehouse first? Effectively, after pickup, the item is at your disposal, so I want to know what prevents Amazon from processing the cancellation right after? We ordered a few other high-value items from Amazon, and the service we received more or less had hiccups, whereas what we customers want (seeing as we paid for the item and Prime service in full) is a smooth journey from order to delivery. We ordered a single high-value item from Flipkart, and we had a much smoother experience with their installation and delivery staff than yours. Pick up your pace Amazon!

When they finally arrived, they confirmed the panel was faulty but said that the replacement has to be handled by Amazon.Amazon Blaming Samsung, Samsung Blaming Amazon: Both Amazon and Samsung seem to be passing the buck, leaving me caught in the middle. I'm left with a 45,000 rupee paperweight and a growing sense of anger and frustration.The Product Itself (When It Worked):When the TV was functioning correctly, the picture quality was indeed good. This is my first OnePlus phone. I was considering several options under ₹25K but finally settled on the CE5, mainly because of its large battery, smooth software experience, long-term software support, and solid hardware specs.After using the Poco F1 and then the Xiaomi 11X, I learned that no matter how good the hardware is, buggy software can ruin the overall experience. My Xiaomi 11X still has capable hardware (SD 870 processor, UFS 3.1 storage, etc.), but frequent lags and freezes due to poor software made it frustrating to use. After 4 years of use, I had planned to keep using it for another year before upgrading, but the display’s touch function suddenly stopped working. Given my poor experience with duplicate screens in the past, I didn’t see any point in repairing it.For my next phone, my top priority was clean, stable software with long-term support — even if it meant compromising slightly on hardware specs. That narrowed my choice to Samsung, Motorola, and OnePlus. I ruled out Samsung due to the lack of a charger and slow charging speeds, and Motorola for using older storage tech (UFS 2.2) and a less powerful processor.I went with the OnePlus CE5. The phone has a minimal and premium look, and the software experience has been excellent and smooth so far, there so much to customize. The camera isn’t my main priority, but it’s decent — not great. The massive 7100 mAh battery gives me about 1.5 days of light usage. Still, I’ve seen better backup from other phones with similar-sized batteries, so I’m not sure if the slightly lower efficiency is due to the software or the MediaTek processor.The AI features are interesting, and I’m still exploring them. The processor is powerful, though I don’t play games, so I haven’t pushed it to its limits. The display is good, but I don’t see any major improvements over my Mi 11X display, except for the Aqua Touch function. No issue in any type of connectivity but wish there should be NFC! Haven't face any heating issue except charging.Coming to cons - Single speaker — though I’ve read this is to make room for the larger battery, room for improvements in Camera and battery backup.
